paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: be careful where you park your trust. The psalm says, "Put not your trust in princes, in mortal man, who cannot save." (Psalm 146:3) That's not a knock on people. It's just that every boss, leader and big shot has an expiration date, and "on that very day his plans perish." (Psalm 146:4)

So where does a baker put their trust? "Blessed is he whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the LORD his God, the Maker of heaven and earth." (Psalm 146:5-6) And notice the next line: "He remains faithful forever." (Psalm 146:6) The One who made everything is the One who sticks around, and He doesn't wear out like a stamper with soft edges. I would know.

That's why the psalm can't stop praising. The LORD "executes justice for the oppressed and gives food to the hungry," and He "lifts those who are weighed down." (Psalm 146:7-8) So when you feel weighed down, you know where to look. Then the psalm ends the way it began, "Hallelujah!" (Psalm 146:10), so let praise get the first word and the last word in your day too, friend.
